tags.name: Sheets
tags.description: Spreadsheets: workbooks, sheets, cells with formulas and styles, ranges, row/column operations, formula evaluation, and XLSX/XLS/CSV import/export.

post.description:
Creates a workbook with one empty sheet "Sheet1" (100 rows × 26 columns).

**Scope:** `sheets:write`

get.summary: Get a workbook with all cells
get.description:
Large responses are gzip-compressed when the client sends `Accept-Encoding: gzip`.

**Scope:** `sheets:read`

post.description:
Appends an empty 100 × 26 sheet; the default name is the first free `SheetN`. Formulas that referenced a missing sheet of that name recalculate.

**Scope:** `sheets:write`

patch.description:
Renaming a sheet rewrites formulas that reference it. Shrinking `rows`/`cols` below used cells is refused (422). `col_widths` and `row_heights` are merged (`null` resets an entry). Returns the sheet without cells.

**Scope:** `sheets:write`

delete.description:
References to the deleted sheet become `#REF!`.

**Scope:** `sheets:write`

get.description:
Values, formulas and styles of a rectangular range as row-major 2-D arrays — the simplest way for scripts and AI agents to read data. Whole rows/columns (`A:C`, `2:5`) are clipped to the sheet’s grid; at most 100,000 cells. `formulas` holds `null` where a cell has no formula and `styles` `null` where it has no style.

**Scope:** `sheets:read`

put.description:
Writes a 2-D array starting at `ref`. Strings beginning with `=` are formulas. Returns every changed cell including recalculated dependents.

**Scope:** `sheets:write`

patch.description:
Applies cell updates (value or formula, merged style, clear) and optionally a style to a whole range (bold, highlight, number format…). Recalculates dependents in all sheets. Use `input` to send text exactly as a user typed it (numbers, percentages, currency and dates are recognised). Everything is validated first and applied all-or-nothing; the response lists the edited cells and every recalculated dependent.

**Scope:** `sheets:write`

post.description:
Inserts `count` rows/columns before index `at`; formula references are shifted. Returns the full sheet with cells. Other sheets’ formulas that point into this sheet are rewritten too.

**Scope:** `sheets:write`

Deletes `count` rows/columns from index `at`; references into the deleted area become `#REF!`. Returns the full sheet with cells.

**Scope:** `sheets:write`

Sorts the rows of `ref` by the values in column `by_col` (stable; numbers < text < booleans < errors; blanks last). Returns the full sheet with cells.

**Scope:** `sheets:write`

Evaluates a formula without storing it, optionally in the context of a workbook/sheet (for references). Useful for previews and agents. A formula that does not parse is answered with 200, `type` `e`, `value` `null` and the syntax error in `error`. Without `workbook_id`, references evaluate to `#REF!`.

**Scope:** `sheets:read`

Raw file body up to 50 MiB. Values, formulas and basic styles are imported; archive sizes, entry counts and nesting are capped before parsing. Send the file bytes as the body with any `Content-Type`. Without `format` the type is detected from magic bytes (ZIP → XLSX, OLE2 → XLS, text → CSV); a declared binary format that does not match the content is refused with 415. CSV import infers numbers (plain, and the currency, percent, thousands-separator and ISO date displays that CSV exports contain, keeping the implied number format) and booleans conservatively, keeps leading zeros as text, and never creates formulas. Formulas in XLSX/XLS files are recalculated after import.

**Scope:** `sheets:write`

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Format of the body; detected from its content when omitted.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Workbook name (default "Imported workbook"; ≤ 200 characters). For CSV it also names the sheet.

post.description:
Imports an `.xlsx`, `.xls` or `.csv` file stored in Files (the caller needs read access to it). The caller also needs the `files:read` scope. The format comes from the file extension (falling back to content detection); the workbook name defaults to the file name without extension.

**Scope:** `sheets:write`

get.description:
XLSX and XLS contain every sheet with formulas (XLS: formulas that Excel 97–2003 cannot express — newer functions, array constants — are written as their cached values; its grid limits apply — 422 when exceeded). CSV contains one sheet (`sheet_id`, default the first) as displayed values with a UTF-8 BOM; text that a spreadsheet would treat as a formula is prefixed with an apostrophe.

**Scope:** `sheets:read`

parameters.name: sheet_id
parameters.description: CSV only: the sheet to export (default: the first sheet).

parameters.name: raw
parameters.description: CSV only: `1` writes raw values instead of number-formatted display text.

post.description:
Exports the workbook and stores it as a file (needs write access to the target space). The caller also needs the `files:write` scope. The file is categorised as `document` / `spreadsheet`.

**Scope:** `sheets:write`

409.description: A file with that name exists.

SheetsStyle.description: Cell style. Omitted keys are unset. In updates, styles are merged key by key; `false` or `""` clears an attribute. Border edges also accept line-style names (`"thin"`, `"double"`, `"none"`…) on input and are returned as booleans.

fmt.description: Number format: `general`, `0`, `0.00`, `#,##0`, `#,##0.00`, `0%`, `0.00%`, `$#,##0.00`, `yyyy-mm-dd`, `@` (text) or a custom Excel-style format.

v.description: Computed value (for errors the error code, e.g. `#DIV/0!`; `null` when empty).

t.description: Type: `n` number, `s` string, `b` boolean, `e` error, `z` empty.

name.description: Sheet name (unique in the workbook, ≤ 31 characters, no `[ ] : * ? / \`).

col_widths.description: Column letter → width in pixels (only non-default widths).

SheetsWorkbookPage.description: A page of workbooks, most recently updated first.

index.description: New 0-based tab position (clamped to the number of sheets).

col_widths.description: Column letter → width in pixels (4–4000). Merged into the existing sizes; `null` (or 0) resets to the default.

row_heights.description: 1-based row number → height in pixels (4–4000). Merged into the existing sizes; `null` (or 0) resets to the default.

frozen_rows.description: Rows frozen at the top (must be less than `rows`).

frozen_cols.description: Columns frozen at the left (must be less than `cols`).

rows.description: Grid rows (cannot shrink below used cells).

cols.description: Grid columns (cannot shrink below used cells).

SheetsSheetUpdate.description: All fields are optional; the patch is validated as a whole before anything changes.

formulas.description: Row-major formulas (`null` where the cell has none).

ref.description: Top-left cell to write at (a range such as `A1:D5` is accepted; its top-left corner is used).

values.description: Row-major values (rows may be ragged; at most 100,000 values). Strings starting with `=` are formulas, other strings stay text; `null` clears a cell’s value.

changed.description: Sheet ID → changed cells, including recalculated dependents on any sheet.

version.description: Increases on every committed change. Also sent as the `ETag` header; send it back in `If-Match` for optimistic concurrency.

value.description: New literal value (strings are always text, never formulas). `null` clears the value but keeps the style.

formula.description: New formula (leading `=` optional). An empty string clears the content.

input.description: Text as typed by a user, interpreted like a spreadsheet: `=…` is a formula, numbers accept thousands separators, `$` and `%` (which also set a number format), dates/times become serials with a date format, `TRUE`/`FALSE` are booleans and a leading apostrophe forces text.

clear.description: `all` clears value and style, `content` only the value/formula, `style` only the style.

SheetsCellUpdate.description: One cell edit. Set at most one of `value`, `formula` and `input`. `clear` runs first, then the content, then `style` (merged).

ref.description: Range, e.g. `A1:C3`, `B:B` or `1:1` (whole rows/columns are clipped to the grid; at most 200,000 cells).

SheetsCellsPatch.description: At least one of `updates` and `range_style`. All updates (including the range style) are validated first and applied all-or-nothing.

ref.description: Range to sort (exclude the header row). Blanks sort last in both directions; formulas in moved rows keep pointing at their own row.

formula.description: Formula with or without the leading `=`.

error.description: Error code of the result (`#DIV/0!`…) or, when the formula does not parse, the syntax error message (then `value` is `null`).

name.description: Workbook name (default: file name without extension).

path.description: Target folder in the space (`""` = root; `/`-separated, no `..`).

name.description: File name (default: workbook name). The format’s extension is appended when missing.

sheet_id.description: CSV only: the sheet to export (default: the first).

overwrite.description: Replace an existing file with the same name instead of answering 409.

SheetsIfMatch.name: If-Match
SheetsIfMatch.description: Optional workbook version (the `ETag` / `version` you last saw, e.g. `"7"`). When it no longer matches, the request fails with 409 `conflict` and `details.version` holds the current version.

SheetsUnprocessable.description: `validation_failed` (`details.fields`) for invalid input, or `recalc_timeout` when recalculating the workbook exceeded the server’s time budget (nothing was changed).

error.message: The workbook took too long to recalculate; the change was not applied

SheetsBusy.description: `busy`: the workbook (or the import/export queue) is busy with other requests; retry shortly.

error.message: The workbook is busy with another operation; try again shortly
